tasks.title: Grayscale
tasks.summary: Turn the screen black and white so apps and icons are less eye-catching.

slides.title: Why grayscale?
slides.body: Apps use bright colors to grab your attention. Without color, red badges and colorful feeds lose a lot of their pull.

media.description: A colorful Home Screen next to the same screen in grayscale

slides.title: Search for Color Filters
slides.body: Open Settings, pull down to reveal the search bar, and search for “Color Filters”.

media.description: Opening Settings and typing “Color Filters” into the search bar

slides.title: Turn on Grayscale
slides.body: Turn on Color Filters and make sure Grayscale is selected.

media.description: Toggling Color Filters on and selecting Grayscale

tasks.title: Reduce Motion
tasks.summary: Tone down zooming and sliding animations across the system.

slides.title: Why reduce motion?
slides.body: Smooth, springy animations make using your phone feel satisfying. Reducing them makes it feel plainer.

media.description: An app opening with the normal zoom animation, then with Reduce Motion's fade

slides.title: Search for Reduce Motion
slides.body: Open Settings and search for “Reduce Motion”.

media.description: Typing “Reduce Motion” into the Settings search bar

slides.title: Turn it on
slides.body: Turn on Reduce Motion.

media.description: Toggling Reduce Motion on

tasks.title: Wallpapers
tasks.summary: Set plain black Home and Lock Screen wallpapers.

slides.title: Go plain
slides.body: A plain black wallpaper gives your eyes nothing to linger on and keeps the focus on what you came to do.

media.description: Lock Screen and Home Screen with plain black wallpapers

slides.title: Search for Wallpaper
slides.body: Open Settings, search for “Wallpaper” and tap Add New Wallpaper.

media.description: Searching “Wallpaper” and tapping Add New Wallpaper

slides.title: Choose black
slides.body: Pick Color, choose black and tap Add. When asked, use it for both the Lock Screen and the Home Screen.

media.description: Choosing Color, selecting black, and setting it as a wallpaper pair

tasks.title: Home Pages
tasks.summary: Clear your Home Screen pages and Today view, and keep new apps in the App Library.

slides.title: Out of sight
slides.body: When apps aren't sitting on your Home Screen, opening one becomes a choice instead of a reflex. Everything stays available in the App Library.

media.description: An empty Home Screen with only the dock

slides.title: Hide your pages
slides.body: Touch and hold the Home Screen until the icons jiggle, tap the page dots at the bottom, and uncheck every page.

media.description: Entering jiggle mode, tapping the page dots, and unchecking pages

slides.title: Clear the Today view
slides.body: Swipe right on the first Home Screen page to reach the Today view. Touch and hold, then remove each widget.

media.description: Removing widgets from the Today view

slides.title: Keep new apps hidden
slides.body: In Settings, search for “Newly Downloaded Apps” and choose App Library Only.

media.description: Searching Settings and selecting App Library Only

tasks.title: Wake & Unlock
tasks.summary: Turn off Raise to Wake, Tap to Wake and Face ID unlock.

slides.title: Make waking deliberate
slides.body: Without these, your phone only lights up and unlocks when you really mean it — no glancing at it every time you pick it up.

media.description: A phone being picked up and the screen staying dark

slides.title: Raise to Wake
slides.body: Open Settings, search for “Raise to Wake” and turn it off.

media.description: Searching “Raise to Wake” and toggling it off

slides.title: Tap to Wake
slides.body: Search for “Tap to Wake” and turn it off.

media.description: Searching “Tap to Wake” and toggling it off

slides.title: Face ID unlock
slides.body: Search for “Face ID & Passcode”, enter your passcode, and turn off iPhone Unlock under Use Face ID For.

media.description: Turning off iPhone Unlock in Face ID & Passcode

tasks.title: Require Passcode
tasks.summary: Ask for your passcode immediately every time the phone locks.

slides.title: No grace period
slides.body: By default your phone may stay unlocked for a few minutes after the screen turns off. Setting this to Immediately means every unlock needs your passcode.

slides.title: Do this after Face ID
slides.body: This option only appears once Face ID unlock is off — with Face ID on, iOS always requires it immediately. Finish Wake & Unlock first.

slides.title: Set it to Immediately
slides.body: In Settings, search for “Face ID & Passcode”, enter your passcode, tap Require Passcode and choose Immediately.

media.description: Setting Require Passcode to Immediately

tasks.title: Long Password
tasks.summary: Use a long alphanumeric passcode so unlocking takes real effort.

slides.title: A little effort goes a long way
slides.body: Typing a long password each time gives you a moment to ask whether you really need your phone right now.

slides.title: Change your passcode
slides.body: In Settings, search for “Face ID & Passcode”, enter your passcode and tap Change Passcode.

media.description: Opening Face ID & Passcode and tapping Change Passcode

slides.title: Choose Custom Alphanumeric
slides.body: Tap Passcode Options, choose Custom Alphanumeric Code, and enter something long that you won't forget.

media.description: Choosing Custom Alphanumeric Code in Passcode Options

tasks.title: Scheduled Summary
tasks.summary: Get non-urgent notifications in batches instead of all day long.

slides.title: Fewer interruptions
slides.body: Scheduled Summary collects notifications from the apps you choose and delivers them together at set times.

media.description: A notification summary on the Lock Screen

slides.title: Search for Scheduled Summary
slides.body: Open Settings, search for “Scheduled Summary” and turn it on.

media.description: Searching “Scheduled Summary” and turning it on

slides.title: Pick times and apps
slides.body: Choose when summaries arrive, then select the apps whose notifications can wait.

media.description: Setting summary times and choosing apps

tasks.title: Notification Badges
tasks.summary: Hide the red counters on app icons so they stop calling you back.

slides.title: Red means urgent — usually it isn't
slides.body: Badges are designed to nag. A red number makes an app feel like it needs you, even when nothing important is waiting.

media.description: App icons with red badges next to the same icons without them

slides.title: Open Notifications
slides.body: Open Settings and tap Notifications. Badges are switched off one app at a time, so start with the apps that pull you in most.

media.description: Opening Settings and tapping Notifications

slides.title: Turn off Badges
slides.body: Tap an app, then turn off Badges. Repeat for every app whose counter you don't need to see.

media.description: Choosing an app in Notifications and toggling Badges off
